response.reason: The cited clause, Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 26(3), directly establishes the requirement that when the country of origin of a food is given and it differs from that of its primary ingredient, the origin of the primary ingredient must also be given or it must be indicated as different. The verdict turns on this exact requirement, assessing whether the specification meets the obligation to clearly communicate the differing origins. Therefore, the clause supports the verdict.
